mainTopic: Eggs and fallen branches between Shabbat and יום טוב, and the two days of יום טוב in the Diaspora and on ראש השנה
overview: This amud first closes the earlier argument about an egg laid on Shabbat when יום טוב comes right after it. Normally the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן against רב, but רבא taught three exceptions where we follow רב, and this egg case is one of them. Next, רבי יוחנן forbids burning branches that fell from a palm tree on Shabbat on the יום טוב that follows. He explains that, unlike the egg, permitting the wood would mislead people into burning wood that fell on יום טוב itself. רב מתנה then rules that branches which fell into an oven on יום טוב may be burned once a majority of prepared wood is added. The גמרא defends this ruling against three challenges: moving forbidden wood, deliberately cancelling a prohibition, and the view of רב אשי. The גמרא then turns to the two days of יום טוב in the Diaspora. רב permits an egg laid on one day to be eaten on the other, and רב אסי forbids it. רבי זירא and אביי argue over whether the second day is based on doubt, and the גמרא concludes that today it is kept as a protective custom of our fathers. Finally, רב and שמואל rule that for the two days of ראש השנה the egg is forbidden on both days, and the גמרא begins quoting a משנה about late witnesses, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the ruling follows רב in the egg case
steps.stepSummary: The sage who delayed his answer explains that had he answered immediately, he would have mistakenly followed רבי יוחנן. But רבא taught that in three cases the הלכה follows רב, and the egg case is one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Had I answered you right then, I would have forgotten and told you: in a dispute between רב and רבי יוחנן, the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן. But רבא said: the הלכה follows רב in these three cases, whether he is lenient or strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the egg discussion. A sage explains why he waited before answering: the usual rule would have led him to the wrong ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that when רב and רבי יוחנן argue, we follow רבי יוחנן. רבא carved out three exceptions in which we follow רב, and the egg laid on Shabbat before יום טוב is one of them. So the egg is forbidden, as רב holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows his opinion

steps.whatToRemember: Usually the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן over רב. In רבא's three exceptional cases, including this egg case, the הלכה follows רב, so the egg is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the general rule that we follow רבי יוחנן against רב. It is only a short list of exceptions.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical ruling: an egg laid on Shabbat may not be eaten on the יום טוב that follows right after it.

phrases.english: Had I [ruled for you] then,
phrases.notes: The sage is explaining why he delayed his answer.

phrases.english: I would have forgotten and said to you:
[In a dispute between] Rav and Rabbi Yochanan —
the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan.
phrases.notes: Under this general rule, the egg would be permitted.

phrases.english: But Rava said:
The halacha follows Rav in these three [cases],
whether leniently or stringently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the egg dispute from the previous part of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the egg case the הלכה follows רב, based on רבא's three exceptions.

steps.title: Branches that fell on Shabbat may not be burned on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that branches which fell from a palm tree on Shabbat may not be used for fuel on the יום טוב that comes the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: branches that fell from a palm tree on Shabbat may not be burned on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן gives a ruling about wood that fell off a tree on Shabbat, when יום טוב comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood that fell on Shabbat could not be used on Shabbat. רבי יוחנן treats Shabbat and the following יום טוב as separate holy days, which is why he permits the egg, so the wood's status does not simply carry over. Even so, he forbids the wood on יום טוב as a safeguard, and steps 4-5 explain why.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sounds surprising, because רבי יוחנן permitted the egg in the same situation. The next steps explain the difference.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Branches that fell from a palm tree on Shabbat —
it is forbidden to burn them on Yom Tov [the next day].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, related to the egg case because it is the same Shabbat-then-יום טוב situation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood that fell on Shabbat is forbidden as fuel on the following יום טוב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן heads off a challenge from the egg
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן anticipates the objection: you permitted the egg, so why not the wood? He then asks what the reason for the difference is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not answer me back with the egg. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן blocks a challenge before anyone raises it: don't ask me why the egg is different. This line sets up his explanation, which comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן himself permitted an egg laid on Shabbat to be eaten on the following יום טוב. So it looks inconsistent to forbid the wood, and he raises that problem himself.

keyTerms.meaning: And do not reply/object to me

phrases.english: And do not reply to me [with] the egg,
phrases.notes: That is, don't object from my lenient ruling about the egg.

phrases.english: What is the reason [for the difference]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible contradiction to the ruling in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling forbidding the wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He permits the egg in the same Shabbat-then-יום טוב situation, so why forbid the wood?

steps.title: Why permitting the egg causes no confusion
steps.stepSummary: An egg could be swallowed raw even on Shabbat, yet it is forbidden that day. So everyone knows it is forbidden on the day it is laid, and permitting it the next day will not mislead anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: An egg: since even on its own day it is fit to be swallowed raw, and still it is not permitted until the next day, it is clearly known that an egg is forbidden on the day it is laid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the egg side of the difference. With an egg, there is no risk that people will misunderstand the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A raw egg could physically be eaten on Shabbat without any cooking, yet it is still forbidden. Because of that, people see clearly that the problem is the egg being new that day, not Shabbat itself. So allowing it on the next day will not make anyone think it is allowed on the day it was laid.

phrases.english: An egg, since on its own day also
it is fit to be swallowed [raw],
phrases.notes: No cooking needed, so Shabbat itself is not what stops it from being eaten.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קָא שָׁרֵי לַהּ עַד לִמְחַר —
phrases.english: and it is not permitted until the next day —
it is clearly known that [the Rabbis] forbade [an egg] on its own day.

steps.triggerLanguage: ביצה משום דביומא נמי חזיא לגומעה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge from step 3 by explaining the egg side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (risk of public confusion)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The egg and the wood are the same case, so they should get the same law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The egg carries no risk of confusion, because its prohibition on the day it is laid is already obvious.

steps.title: Why permitting the wood would cause confusion
steps.stepSummary: Wood could not be burned on Shabbat anyway. If we permitted it on the next day, people would think the only problem was Shabbat, and they would burn wood that fell on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wood, which was not usable on its own day: if you permit it the next day, people will come to say that on its own day it is also permitted, and that yesterday it was unusable for burning only because of Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his explanation with the wood side. Permitting the wood would lead people to a mistaken conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting a fire is forbidden on Shabbat, so no one saw the wood being treated as forbidden for its own sake. If we allowed it on יום טוב, people would assume Shabbat was the only obstacle. Then they would wrongly burn wood that fell on a יום טוב itself, so the wood is forbidden as a safeguard.

keyTerms.meaning: They will come to say (mistakenly conclude)

steps.whatToRemember: The egg is permitted but the wood is forbidden because of the risk of confusion. The egg's prohibition is obvious; the wood's prohibition would be mistaken for a mere Shabbat issue.

phrases.english: Wood, which was not usable on its own day,
if you permit it the next day —
people will come to say:
on their own day too, they are permitted,
and yesterday, it was because of Shabbat
that they were not usable for burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the distinction begun in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (risk of public confusion)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the egg is permitted, the wood should be too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wood is forbidden as a safeguard against people thinking that wood which falls on יום טוב may be burned that same day.

steps.title: Fallen branches in an oven can be outnumbered by prepared wood
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה rules that if branches fell into an oven on יום טוב, one may add more prepared wood and burn it all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: branches that fell from a palm tree into an oven on יום טוב: one adds prepared wood on top of them and burns them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new related ruling. רב מתנה gives a practical solution for forbidden branches that landed right inside an oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches that fell on יום טוב were not prepared before the holiday, so they are מוקצה and may not be used. רב מתנה says that by adding a larger amount of permitted, prepared wood, one may light the whole pile.

keyTerms.meaning: Adds more on top of them

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
Branches that fell from a palm tree
into the oven on Yom Tov —
one adds prepared wood on top of them,
and burns them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling on the same subject of fallen branches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fallen מוקצה branches in an oven may be burned once a majority of prepared wood is added.

steps.title: But he is moving forbidden wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב מתנה: while burning, a person stirs and turns the wood, so he is handling the forbidden branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is turning over forbidden [wood]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב מתנה's ruling. During cooking you poke and turn the fire, which means moving מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving מוקצה on יום טוב is forbidden. Even if lighting the pile is fine, stirring the fire would mean touching and moving the forbidden branches.

phrases.english: But he is turning over forbidden [wood]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב מתנה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנה's permission to burn the mixed wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stirring the fire moves מוקצה wood, which is forbidden.

steps.title: The majority makes it all permitted wood
steps.stepSummary: Since most of the wood is permitted, the forbidden pieces are cancelled by the majority, so he is considered to be moving permitted wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since most of it is permitted wood, when he turns it over, he is turning over permitted wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge using the rule of majority (רוב).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once permitted wood outnumbers the forbidden wood, the forbidden pieces lose their status inside the mix. So stirring the pile counts as moving permitted wood.

phrases.english: Since the majority is permitted [wood],
when he turns it over —
he is turning over permitted [wood].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Application of a legal principle (majority nullifies)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He is handling forbidden מוקצה wood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden wood is nullified by the majority, so it counts as permitted.

steps.title: But you may not cancel a prohibition on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: adding wood deliberately cancels the forbidden wood, and a משנה teaches that one may not cancel a prohibited item on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is cancelling a forbidden item deliberately, and we learned in a משנה: one may not cancel a forbidden item deliberately!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that majority works, but now attacks how the majority came about: it was created on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nullification by majority normally works when the mix happens by accident. Here the person is deliberately adding permitted wood in order to cancel the forbidden wood. A משנה forbids exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not deliberately nullify a prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge does not deny that a majority cancels forbidden items. It only objects to creating that majority on purpose.

phrases.english: But he is nullifying a forbidden item deliberately,
and we learned [in a mishnah]:
One may not nullify a forbidden item deliberately!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of majority to permit the wood in step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The majority was deliberately created, which a משנה forbids.

steps.title: Deliberate cancelling is only forbidden for Torah prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The rule against deliberately cancelling a prohibition applies only to Torah-level prohibitions. Rabbinic prohibitions like מוקצה may be cancelled on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only to Torah prohibitions, but with rabbinic prohibitions one may nullify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by limiting the משנה's rule to Torah-level prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוקצה is a rabbinic prohibition, so the ban on deliberate nullification does not apply to it. That is why רב מתנה's method of adding prepared wood is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: רב מתנה's ruling stands: a majority of prepared wood cancels fallen מוקצה branches, and creating that majority on purpose is allowed because מוקצה is only rabbinic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a widely used principle: אין מבטלין איסור לכתחילה applies to Torah prohibitions, but not to rabbinic ones (according to this גמרא).

phrases.english: These words apply to Torah [prohibitions],
but with rabbinic [prohibitions], one may nullify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule (Torah vs. rabbinic)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Deliberate nullification is forbidden for every prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Deliberate nullification is forbidden only for Torah prohibitions, and מוקצה is rabbinic.

steps.title: How does this work for רב אשי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב מתנה's ruling fits with רב אשי, who holds that anything that will become permitted later is never cancelled, even in a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב אשי, who said that anything that will become permitted later is not cancelled, even in a rabbinic prohibition, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up רב אשי's rule and asks how the answer in Step 10 can work for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said that a rabbinic prohibition like מוקצה may be cancelled on purpose. But רב אשי holds that a דבר שיש לו מתירין is never cancelled, even when the prohibition is only rabbinic. These branches will become permitted after יום טוב, so for רב אשי they should never be cancelled by the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: An item that will become permitted later on its own (here, after יום טוב)
Is not cancelled by a majority
What can be said? (a challenge formula)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב אשי with רב אסי, who appears later here. They are different אמוראים.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Ashi, who said:
Any item that will become permitted later
even in a rabbinic prohibition, is not cancelled,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 10 using a different אמורא's view on ביטול
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the forbidden branches are cancelled by the majority (Steps 8 and 10)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The branches can be burned after יום טוב, so they are a דבר שיש לו מתירין. According to רב אשי, such an item is never cancelled, even in a rabbinic prohibition.

steps.title: The forbidden wood is already burning
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's rule applies only when the forbidden item stays whole. Here the forbidden wood is being burned up.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies only where the forbidden item stays intact. Here, the forbidden item is being burned up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב אשי's rule does not apply here, because the forbidden wood is burning away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of דבר שיש לו מתירין applies to an item that stays whole and recognizable. When the person stirs the fire, the branches are already burning or turning into coals. So he is not really handling an intact forbidden item, and רב מתנה's ruling works even for רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only (limits a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: רב מתנה's ruling holds according to everyone. Most אמוראים allow it because rabbinic prohibitions may be cancelled. רב אשי allows it because the forbidden wood is burned up and no longer intact.

phrases.english: These words apply only where
the forbidden item remains intact,
here, the forbidden item is being burned up.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ לְאִיסּוּרָא בְּעֵינֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by limiting רב אשי's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule (distinguishing the case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי's rule should block cancelling the branches, since they become permitted after יום טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אשי's rule applies only to an intact forbidden item. Burning wood is not intact, so the ruling stands.

steps.title: רב and רב אסי on an egg laid on one of the two days
steps.stepSummary: There is a dispute about the two days of יום טוב in the Diaspora. רב permits an egg laid on one day to be eaten on the other day. רב אסי forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Regarding the two days of יום טוב in the Diaspora, רב said an egg laid on one day is permitted on the other. רב אסי said an egg laid on one day is forbidden on the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic and records a dispute between רב and רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg laid on יום טוב is forbidden that day (the topic of this מסכת). In the Diaspora, יום טוב is kept for two days because of doubt about the date. רב reasons that one of the days is surely a weekday, so an egg laid on one day may be eaten on the other. רב אסי forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: The two days of יום טוב kept outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר: שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל גָּלִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: It was stated: the two Festival days of the Diaspora,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: נוֹלְדָה בָּזֶה — מוּתֶּרֶת בָּזֶה,
phrases.english: Rav said: an egg laid on this day is permitted on that day,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: נוֹלְדָה בָּזֶה — אֲסוּרָה בָּזֶה.
phrases.english: and Rav Asi said: an egg laid on this day is forbidden on that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל גָּלִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the burning wood discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: an egg laid on one day of יום טוב של גליות is permitted on the other. רב אסי: it is forbidden.

steps.title: Does רב אסי treat both days as one holiness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב אסי sees the two days as one holiness. It then challenges this, because רב אסי made הבדלה between the two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say רב אסי holds that the two days are one holiness? But רב אסי himself made הבדלה from one יום טוב to the next!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא guesses the reason for רב אסי's view, and then attacks that reason using his own practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding the egg on the second day suggests that רב אסי treats both days as one long holy day (קדושה אחת). But הבדלה marks the end of a holy day, and he made הבדלה between the first and second day. That act treats the days as two separate holinesses, so his practice seems to contradict his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: One single holiness (both days counted as one)
Makes הבדלה (separating holy time from the next day)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Asi holds
that it is one holiness?
But Rav Asi makes havdalah
from one Festival day to the other!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא קָא סָבַר רַב אַסִּי קְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the reason for רב אסי's ruling in Step 13 and finds a contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling forbidding the egg
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His ruling implies the two days are one holiness. His הבדלה between the days implies they are two separate holinesses. Both cannot be true.

steps.title: רב אסי was unsure, so he was strict both ways
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי was in doubt whether the days are one holiness or two, so he followed the strict side in each case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי was in doubt, so he acted strictly here and strictly there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב אסי did not hold firmly either way. Because he was unsure, he was strict in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי did not decide whether the two days are one holiness or two. For the egg, he was strict as if the days were one holiness, and forbade it. For הבדלה, he was strict as if the days were two holinesses, and said it. Both practices come from the same doubt, so there is no contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי's two practices are consistent. He was unsure whether the two days of יום טוב are one holiness or two, so he was strict in each case: no egg from the other day, and הבדלה between the days.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אסי did not decide that the days are one holiness, and he did not decide they are two. Each strict practice only covers one side of his doubt.

phrases.english: Rav Asi was in doubt,
and he acted stringently here
and stringently here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the opinion as a doubt rather than a firm position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי firmly holds the two days are one holiness, which clashes with his הבדלה
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אסי is in doubt, so he is strict in both directions: he forbids the egg and he makes הבדלה.

steps.title: רבי זירא supports רב אסי from today's practice
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says רב אסי's view makes sense. Today we know the calendar exactly, and we still keep two days of יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It makes sense to follow רב אסי. Nowadays we know when the month begins, and yet we still keep two days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a logical support for רב אסי's strict view, which forbids the egg on the second day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second day were only about doubt, it should have stopped once the calendar became known. Since we still keep it, it looks like a real, fixed holiness, and not just a 'maybe this is the day.' That supports treating the two days strictly, as רב אסי does.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with him / like his view
It is reasonable / it makes sense
The fixing of the month (when רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ falls)

steps.confusionAlert: In step 15 the גמרא said רב אסי himself was in doubt. רבי זירא is not repeating that. He is giving his own reason why the strict side of רב אסי is sensible: the second day no longer looks like a pure doubt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It is reasonable to follow Rav Asi,
for nowadays we know the fixing of the month,
phrases.notes: There is a set calendar, so no one is unsure when the festival falls.

phrases.english: and yet we keep two days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב אסי's position has been explained, רבי זירא adds logical support for it.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's strict ruling that the egg from one day is forbidden on the other day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Present-day practice: we keep two days even though the calendar is known.

steps.title: אביי supports רב from the משנה about torches and messengers
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב's view makes sense. He quotes a משנה: first they lit torches to announce the new month, and after the כותים disrupted this, messengers were sent instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense to follow רב. As we learned in a משנה: At first they would light torches. Once the כותים ruined this, the Rabbis arranged for messengers to go out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues the opposite of רבי זירא. He quotes a משנה to show that the second day comes from doubt, which supports רב's lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows the history. The torch signal was replaced by slow messengers, and far-away communities could not be sure which day was the festival. That uncertainty is the real source of the second day. So one day is the true festival and the other is kept only out of doubt. They are not one holiness.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is reasonable to follow Rav,
as we learned in a Mishnah: At first,
they would light torches,
phrases.notes: Fires on the mountaintops announced that the new month had been declared.

phrases.english: once the Samaritans ruined this,
phrases.notes: They lit torches on the wrong days to confuse people.

phrases.english: they instituted that messengers should go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a counter-argument to רבי זירא. It supports רב instead of רב אסי.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the two days are separate, so an egg from one day is permitted on the other.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (ראש השנה 22b) about torches being replaced by messengers.

steps.title: אביי's inference: without the doubt, only one day would be kept
steps.stepSummary: אביי draws the conclusion from the משנה. If the כותים had stopped, or wherever the messengers arrived in time, only one day would be kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the כותים had stopped, we would keep one day. And wherever the messengers reached, we keep one day.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof by pointing out what follows from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second day depends entirely on whether people know the correct date. Take away the confusion, and the second day disappears. This shows the second day is a doubt-based safeguard, which fits רב.

phrases.english: And if the Samaritans had stopped —
we would keep one day,
and where the messengers arrive —
we keep one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes אביי's proof by drawing the conclusion from the משנה he quoted.
steps.raayaObject: That the second day exists only because of doubt, which supports רב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from the משנה: no confusion means one day.

steps.title: Then why do we keep two days today?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי. If the second day is only about doubt, why do we still keep it now that we know the calendar?
steps.simpleTranslation: But now that we know the fixing of the month, what is the reason we keep two days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem for אביי's view using the same fact רבי זירא pointed out. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the doubt is the whole reason for the second day. Today the doubt is gone, so the second day should be gone too. Yet we still keep it, so that needs an explanation.

phrases.english: And now that we know the fixing of the month,
what is the reason we keep two days?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּיָדְעִינַן בִּקְבִיעָא דְיַרְחָא, מַאי טַעְמָא עָבְדִינַן תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This tests אביי's view against the present-day fact raised by רבי זירא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the second day is based only on doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Today there is no doubt, yet the practice continues. So the practice seems to stand on something other than doubt.

steps.title: A warning from ארץ ישראל: keep your fathers' custom
steps.stepSummary: We keep two days because ארץ ישראל sent word to hold on to the custom of our fathers. Persecution might one day make the calendar get lost and cause confusion again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they sent from there (ארץ ישראל): Be careful with the custom of your fathers that is in your hands. Sometimes the government makes a decree, and things may come to be ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Today the second day is kept as a protective custom, not because of a real present-day doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes רבי זירא's support for רב אסי. The fact that we keep two days today does not prove the second day is a fixed holiness. It is kept only as a protective custom. At its root, the second day is still based on doubt, which fits רב.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there (from אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל)
A decree (here, a decree of persecution)
To go wrong / to be ruined

steps.whatToRemember: The second day of יום טוב in the Diaspora began because of doubt about the date. Today it continues as a binding custom from our fathers, kept as protection in case the calendar is ever forgotten. It is not kept because of any doubt today.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second day is optional just because it is called a 'custom.' ארץ ישראל specifically warned the Diaspora to keep it. It is binding. The question here is only about its root: is it a doubt, or one holiness?
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for why the Diaspora still keeps two days of יום טוב even with a fixed calendar.

phrases.english: Because they sent from there:
Be careful with the custom of your fathers that is in your hands,
sometimes the government will issue a decree,
phrases.notes: For example, a ban on Torah study that could cause the calendar to be forgotten.

phrases.english: and they will come to err.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge in step 19 and protects אביי's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: It gives a new reason for the current practice. Today's two days come from a safeguarding custom, not from a doubt about the date.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Keeping two days today proves the second day is one fixed holiness, as רבי זירא argued for רב אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The practice continues only as a protective custom. Its original basis was doubt, which fits רב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two days are kept today because of a warning from ארץ ישראל to preserve the custom of our fathers. This leaves the second day's root in doubt, which supports רב.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: an egg laid on one day of ראש השנה is forbidden on the other
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל both rule that for the two days of ראש השנה, an egg laid on the first day is forbidden on the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about the two יום טוב days of ראש השנה, רב and שמואל both said: if an egg was laid on one day, it is forbidden on the other day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new related discussion about ראש השנה and gives a ruling from רב and שמואל together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, about the two days of יום טוב kept outside ארץ ישראל, רב allowed an egg laid on one day to be eaten on the other. Those two days are treated as two separate holy days, and one of them is really a regular weekday. Here even רב agrees that ראש השנה is different. Its two days are treated like one long holy day, so the egg stays forbidden on both.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year festival, kept for two days
An egg laid on this day is forbidden on that day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב is contradicting himself. He allowed the egg for the two days of יום טוב outside ארץ ישראל, but ראש השנה is a special case with its own reason. That reason comes in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the well-known idea that the two days of ראש השנה are treated as one long day. That idea affects many הלכות, not just eggs.

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר, שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: It was stated: about the two Festival days of Rosh Hashana,
Rav and Shmuel both said:
phrases.notes: Even רב, who was lenient about the two days outside ארץ ישראל, agrees here.

phrases.english: An egg laid on this day is forbidden on that day,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two days of יום טוב outside ארץ ישראל to the special case of ראש השנה, where the ruling is stricter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the two days of ראש השנה, an egg laid on one day is forbidden on the other.

steps.title: The משנה about late witnesses for the new month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה as the source for רב and שמואל. Long ago, בית דין accepted witnesses of the new moon all day long, until once the witnesses came late.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: at first, בית דין would accept testimony about the new month for the whole day. One time, the witnesses were delayed in coming,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a משנה to support רב and שמואל. This step only sets up the story; the משנה continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the 30th day of אלול, nobody knew in advance whether that day would become ראש השנה. It depended on witnesses arriving to say they saw the new moon. Because of this, the day was treated as holy from the start, even in ארץ ישראל. The story of the late witnesses will show how this led to a fixed custom of two days that count as one.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony of witnesses who saw the new moon

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Originally, they would accept
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in ראש השנה 30b.

phrases.english: testimony of the new month the entire day.
phrases.notes: Witnesses could come any time on the 30th day, and the day would become the new month.

phrases.english: Once, the witnesses were delayed in coming,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reason for רב and שמואל's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב and שמואל's ruling that the two days of ראש השנה are treated as one, so the egg is forbidden on both.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ראש השנה 30b about how witnesses of the new moon were accepted, and the time they came late.
